Maya,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the PDF. A couple of clarifications from our security and identity teams before we mark the questionnaire complete:

1) SCIM: You note support for SCIM 2.0. Do you support performant bulk provisioning for >200k users across multiple tenants? Specifically, do you provide chunked bulk endpoints or rely on delta sync only? Also what are typical rate limits and backoff behavior?

2) Delegated admin: Can you describe the exact boundaries for delegated admins (what can they create vs. what is tenant-only)? Is there a separate audit trail for actions taken by delegated admins? Retention of those logs?

3) SSO Attributes: For SAML assertions we need to confirm attribute mappings for nameID/email, groups, and custom attributes used for entitlements. Do you support OIDC claim mapping as well?

4) Evidence: Can you share a simple diagram of your SCIM provisioning architecture showing bulk vs incremental flows (if available)?

We’re targeting the technical review on Friday; if you can provide answers/attachments by Wednesday EOD EDT that will keep us on schedule.

Thanks,
Elaine
Senior IT Security Manager

Maya/Kimberly — answers and artifacts below; attaching a compact diagram and an admin-role matrix workbook. Attachment stubs listed at bottom.

SCIM (summary):
- We support SCIM 2.0 with two complementary patterns: a) chunked bulk provisioning endpoints for onboarding large directories (POST /scim/v2/Bulk) and b) standard delta-based /Users endpoint for incremental updates. The bulk path accepts up to 10k records per chunk by default; customers can request higher chunk sizes for dedicated deployments. The bulk API returns an async job ID and a chunk status endpoint for progress.
- For multi-tenant customers with >200k identities, we recommend chunked bulk + per-tenant partitioning. In Dedicated/Private deployments we can increase concurrency to meet onboarding windows.
- Rate limits: default tenant policy is 60 requests/minute for SCIM non-bulk endpoints; bulk endpoints are metered by concurrent jobs (default 4 jobs/tenant). Exponential backoff (retry-after header + 2^n) is enforced for 429s. These values are configurable for Dedicated customers under the SLA.

Delegated admin and RBAC:
- Admin roles are hierarchical: Super Admin (org-level), Tenant Admin, Application Admin, Delegated Support Admin. Delegated Support Admin can manage user lifecycle (create/update/deactivate) but cannot change org-wide network or billing settings.
- Delegated admin actions are logged with full actor/context: action, target resource, timestamp, IP, and session id.
- Audit retention: default 90 days; enterprise packages include 1yr/3yr retention and exportable WORM storage. Audit logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM (syslog/HTTPS) or pushed to customer-managed cloud storage.

SAML/OIDC attribute mapping:
- SAML: we support customizable attribute mapping (NameID format, urn:mace:dir:attribute-def for standard attributes). Example mapping: NameID -> email; urn:custom:entitlement -> app_entitlements.
- OIDC: claim mapping supported via JSON paths; custom claims can be emitted on token issue. Token translation/proxy available for legacy IdPs.

Encryption/KMS/HSM:
- Customer-managed keys supported for data at rest encryption and for signing artifacts in Private deployments (KMS integration via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault; HSM options on prem).

Attachments (stubs included):
- saml_scim_diagram.png (SCIM bulk vs incremental flow, async job lifecycle)
- admin_role_matrix.xlsx (matrix of roles, allowed actions, example delegations)
- novara_iam_questionnaire_filled.pdf (finalized answers in questionnaire format)

If you want I can add a short example curl flow for a bulk job and an example SAML attribute-mapping snippet.

Connor

Elaine/Raj —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Please find our consolidated answers and artifacts attached: novara_iam_questionnaire_filled.pdf, saml_scim_diagram.png, admin_role_matrix.xlsx. Highlights below:

- SCIM: Redwood supports both chunked bulk (async) and incremental (delta) workflows. Bulk supports configurable chunk sizes (default 10k) and concurrent job limits; for Dedicated deployments we can raise concurrency and chunk size to meet >200k onboarding windows. We expose job/status endpoints and advise per-tenant partitioning for scale. Rate limits and retry semantics are documented in the attached PDF; defaults are adjustable under an SLA.

- Delegated admin & RBAC: Delegated Support Admins can handle user lifecycle but not org-level settings. All delegated actions produce detailed audit records (actor, resource, action, IP, session id) and audit retention can be extended to 1/3 years with exportable WORM storage or SIEM forwarding.

- SAML/OIDC mapping: both SAML attribute mapping and OIDC claim mapping are supported; we included examples and a small snippet you can drop into your IdP mapping rules.

- Encryption & keys: Customer-managed KMS supported for private deployments. Audit logs can be encrypted and stored under customer keys where required.
